free_tier.stated: Free with no account: a public HTTPS URL per tunnel, a 3-hour session window and 1 GiB of traffic per session on the anonymous tier. A free account removes the session window and allows 3 GiB per UTC day; paid plans have a full-speed allowance that refills continuously, and sustained use beyond it continues at a reduced rate.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: a tunnel, not an object

retention.stated: not applicable: a live tunnel; an anonymous session ends after 3 hours

egress.terms: 1 GiB per session on the anonymous tier and 3 GiB per UTC day on the free account; past the cap visitors get an HTTP 429 page. Paid plans have a continuously refilling full-speed allowance, 750 GB on Basic and 1.5 TB on Pro, and continue at a reduced rate beyond it.; ingress: http
egress.free_allowance: 1 GiB per session (anonymous); 3 GiB per UTC day (free account)

interface_detail: cruma proxy http <host:port> prints a public https://<id>.tun.cruma.io URL; the desktop app and the local reverse proxy use the same agent
tooling: the cruma CLI from npm (@cruma-io/cli) or the desktop app; the agent is also a local web server and reverse proxy
chaining: one anonymous tunnel publishes a webhook receiver or a small HTTP service; it carries TCP only, and the 1 GiB session cap makes it a test lane rather than a service lane

limits.value: 1 GiB per session on the anonymous tier
a 3-hour session window on the anonymous tier
past the cap visitors get an HTTP 429 page

binding_note: the session byte cap fails first: 1 GiB is one large file, and the 3-hour window ends the tunnel even when the bytes are unspent.

identity_cost.detail: no account: the homepage says 'Free · no account needed'; a free account is optional and raises the daily cap to 3 GiB

reliability_note: an anonymous session ends after 3 hours and 1 GiB; a capability-free sandbox measured a 329 ms median latency and 117-126 kB/s on a 4 MiB transfer on 2026-11-05
confidence_note: the anonymous tier's limits are read from the vendor pricing page; the latency and throughput are a sandbox measurement and are recorded as such

evidence.proved: the anonymous tier is a 3-hour session with 1 GiB of traffic
past the cap visitors get an HTTP 429 page
evidence.quote: past the cap, visitors get an HTTP 429 page

evidence.proved: the free account allows 3 GiB per UTC day
evidence.quote: Free tunnels at 3 GiB per UTC day

evidence.proved: no account is needed for a free tunnel
a 4 MiB transfer completed at 117-126 kB/s and /lat returned 200

notes: The fastest hosted relay by its own harness's account in a 2026-11-05 benchmark of authless relays: 329 ms median latency (probe sha256:e3b9e671b9637952dcd876c4cad821a9d4e22a5d44064934190f68c60fd1a133). The anonymous tier is a development allowance of 3 hours and 1 GiB per session, not a service tier.
